\section{Round-eight reconstruction: dynamic action, resolvent graph core, and two-scale comparison}
\label{sec:r8-b4}

Static preparation is charged once in the initial boundary functional.  The
transition action contains only dynamic contact entropy.  Smooth graph-core
approximation uses resolvents of the actual generator, not an impossible
analytic cutoff.  Comparison uses a slope-capped penalty whose coercivity is
sent to infinity in a separate limit.

\subsection{Dynamic-only transition action}

For a compatible path $(f,\Gamma)$ on $[s,t]$ set
\[
 \mathcal A_{s,t}(f,\Gamma)
 =\int_s^t\int\ell\!\left(\frac{d\Gamma}{dA_f}\right)dA_f\,dr,
 \qquad \ell(q)=q\log q-q+1.
\]
The preparation rate $I_0(f_s)$ is not part of $\mathcal A_{s,t}$.

\begin{lemma}[Exact cocycle of dynamic cost]
\label{lem:r8-b4-cost}
For every compatible path and $s<u<t$,
\[
 \mathcal A_{s,t}=\mathcal A_{s,u}+\mathcal A_{u,t}.
\]
Consequently the Lax--Oleinik operators
\[
 (V_t\varphi)(f)=\sup\{\varphi(f_t)-\mathcal A_{0,t}:f_0=f\}
\]
satisfy $V_{t+s}=V_tV_s$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The action is an integral over time, so additivity is exact.  Concatenation of
compatible paths preserves the B2 graph trace at the joining time.  Splitting
and concatenating competitors proves both semigroup inequalities.  A static
rate can be applied once to an initial distribution, but is never recharged at
the intermediate state.
\end{proof}

\subsection{A resolvent-generated graph core}

Let $\mathbb A_\varepsilon$ be the closed augmented BBGKY generator on the
law/contact-ledger state and
\[
 J_{\lambda,\varepsilon}=(I-\lambda\mathbb A_\varepsilon)^{-1}.
\]
For a finite coordinate projection $\Pi_m$ and
$\phi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^m)$ define
\[
 F_{m,\lambda}(z)=\phi(\Pi_mJ_{\lambda,\varepsilon}z).
\]

\begin{lemma}[Smooth bounded graph core]
\label{lem:r8-b4-core}
The algebra generated by $F_{m,\lambda}$ lies in the generator graph domain,
is stable under products, and is dense on every action compactum in the
$C_b^2$ cylinder graph norm as $m\to\infty$ and $\lambda\downarrow0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The resolvent maps the state space into $D(\mathbb A_\varepsilon)$ and satisfies
$\mathbb A_\varepsilon J_\lambda=
\lambda^{-1}(J_\lambda-I)$.  The chain rule gives bounded graph images because
$\phi$ has compactly supported derivatives.  The Markov generator product
formula on its resolvent range gives stability under products.  Compact
containment makes finitely many coordinates uniformly separating; Stone--Weierstrass
approximates the cylinder, and $J_\lambda\to I$ uniformly on the compactum.
No analytic function is required to equal one on an open box and change
outside it.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Exact finite-generator correctors}

Let $V_\varepsilon(t,s)$ be the backward observable propagator of the actual
finite augmented generator along a smooth reference path:
\[
 \partial_tV_\varepsilon(t,s)
 =-\mathbb A_\varepsilon(t)V_\varepsilon(t,s),
 \qquad V_\varepsilon(s,s)=I.
\]
For the order-$j$ defect $D_j^\varepsilon$ define
\[
 c_j^\varepsilon(t)=\int_t^T
 V_\varepsilon(t,s)D_j^\varepsilon(s)\,ds.
\]

\begin{theorem}[Finite graph-domain Poisson corrector]
\label{thm:r8-b4-corrector}
Each corrector belongs to the finite generator graph domain and satisfies
\[
 \partial_tc_j^\varepsilon+
 \mathbb A_\varepsilon(t)c_j^\varepsilon=-D_j^\varepsilon,
 \qquad c_j^\varepsilon(T)=0.
\]
For suitable ledger weights,
\[
 \sum_{j\ge0}\sup_{t\le T}
 \bigl(\|c_j^\varepsilon(t)\|+
 \|\mathbb A_\varepsilon c_j^\varepsilon(t)\|\bigr)<\infty
\]
uniformly in $\varepsilon$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The propagator is constructed by forward Picard iteration in remaining time
and preserves the graph domain by the B2 boundary-renewal estimate.
Differentiating the Duhamel integral gives the equation and the exact zero
terminal value.  A defect with $j$ ledger labels carries the cluster factor
$C^j/j!$; choose the ledger radius below the graph-semigroup radius and sum the
resulting exponential series, including the generator images.
\end{proof}

\subsection{A two-scale slope-capped penalty}

Let $d_B$ be a bounded-compatible metric on an energy containment set.  Choose
$\omega\in C^2([0,\infty))$ increasing, $\omega(r)=r$ for $r\le1$, and
$0\le\omega'\le1$.  For $R\ge1$ and $\eta>0$ put
\[
 \Psi_{R,\eta}(f,g)=\frac{R}{\eta}\omega(\eta d_B(f,g)).
\]
For fixed $R$, its cotangent norm is at most $R$.  Coercivity is obtained by
$R\to\infty$, not by falsely claiming that $\eta\downarrow0$ makes a bounded
distance diverge.

\begin{lemma}[Diagonal localization with bounded slopes]
\label{lem:r8-b4-penalty}
At a doubled maximum of
$u(f)-v(g)-\Psi_{R,\eta}(f,g)$ on a common containment set,
\[
 d_B(f,g)\le C/R+o_\eta(1),
\]
while both test cotangents lie in the Hamiltonian source ball of radius $R$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Compare the maximum with the diagonal point $f=g$.  Since $u,v$ are bounded,
$\Psi_{R,\eta}(f,g)\le C$.  For $\eta d_B\le1$ the penalty is $Rd_B$; if
this inequality fails, first choose $\eta$ small on the bounded metric space.
Thus $d_B\le C/R$.  Differentiation gives slope
$R\omega'(\eta d_B)\le R$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Comparison on the full state space]
\label{thm:r8-b4-comparison}
Assume the Hamiltonian is continuous on every bounded cotangent ball and obeys
the exponential containment bound supplied by B2.  Then bounded upper and
lower viscosity solutions of the Hamilton--Jacobi equation satisfy comparison.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Fix $R$ and apply the doubled-variable argument with
$\Psi_{R,\eta}$.  Lemma~\ref{lem:r8-b4-penalty} keeps the two cotangents inside
the radius-$R$ chart.  Let $\eta\downarrow0$ to remove smoothing of the metric.
The states are then within $C/R$.  Hamiltonian continuity on the radius-$R$
chart makes the state mismatch vanish as $R\to\infty$; exponential containment
removes the complement before this limit.  The standard viscosity inequalities
then contradict a positive maximum.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Nonlinear semigroup convergence}

\begin{theorem}[Microscopic-to-kinetic nonlinear semigroups]
\label{thm:r8-b4-convergence}
The logarithmic microscopic semigroups on the augmented law/contact-ledger state
converge locally uniformly on action compacta to the dynamic Lax--Oleinik
semigroup generated by $\mathcal A$.  The limit is unique and satisfies the
semigroup law.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Use the graph core of Lemma~\ref{lem:r8-b4-core} and the exact correctors of
Theorem~\ref{thm:r8-b4-corrector} to obtain generator convergence with no
terminal remainder.  B2 gives compact containment and lower recovery for the
dynamic action.  Half-relaxed limits are viscosity sub- and supersolutions.
The comparison theorem identifies them.  Lemma~\ref{lem:r8-b4-cost} supplies
the semigroup law and prevents double charging of preparation.
\end{proof}
